sections.title: Read the passage and fill in the blanks.

questions.q: Rembrandt was a ______ painter.
The varnish on The Night Watch was removed in ______.
The captain is dressed in black with a ______ sash.
The lieutenant and the small girl wear ______ dress, the colour of victory.
The dead chicken hanging from the girl's belt represents the ______.

sections.passage: Rembrandt was a Dutch painter and a realist. In most of his paintings we see the mysteries in the play of light and shade. He painted The Night Watch between 1640 and 1642. For a long time the painting was coated with dark varnish, which gave the incorrect impression that it depicted a night scene, but when the varnish was removed in 1940 it was found to represent broad daylight. The captain is dressed in black with a red sash. The lieutenant and a small girl wear yellow, the colour of victory. A white dead chicken hanging from the girl's belt represents the defeated enemy.

sections.title: Read the passage and state whether each statement is true or false.

questions.q: Pieta was carved from a single slab of marble.
Pieta has three figures.
questions.answer: False – it has two figures, Mary and Christ.

questions.q: The structure of Pieta is pyramidal.
Michelangelo painted the frescoes on the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel.

sections.passage: Pieta is a sculpture made by Michael Angelo in 1498–99. It is created from a single slab of marble. It shows the Virgin Mary holding the dead body of Christ in her hands. The structure of this sculpture is pyramidal in shape. Madonna is shown much younger than her son to express her purity. This is the most highly finished work of Michael Angelo. The other famous works of Michael Angelo are the sculptures of David and Moses and the frescoes on the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel in Rome.

questions.q: What are the characteristics of Ajanta paintings?
questions.answer: They were done in two phases (Hinayana – Buddha in symbols; Mahayana – in human form) in tempera, not fresco. The themes are mainly religious but have scope for creativity; women are shown beautifully; the line is flowing, the colours are earthy and the paintings can be enjoyed by common people.

questions.q: When did Wassily Kandinsky paint 'Black Lines'?
What does the painting 'Hamsa Damayanti' depict?
questions.answer: It shows Damayanti in a red sari lovingly listening to the messages of her lover Nala narrated by a swan (hamsa); her silent love is shown in the sparkle of her eyes and the glow of her cheeks.

questions.q: What do you know about the Indian painter who became blind?
questions.answer: Benode Behari Mukherjee, a student of Nandalal Bose, had weak eyesight from childhood and became totally blind later but still created a huge mural at Kala Bhavan, Santiniketan, including 'The Mediaeval Saints' in Fresco Buono at Hindi Bhavan.

sections.title: Short answer question. Answer in 50–60 words.

questions.q: Write the main characteristics of Hoysala sculptures.
questions.answer: They show deep carving and undercutting made possible by the soft schist stone, rich surface texture, soft rhythms of body contours and delicate intricate designs; sculptures are part of the temple architecture; examples are at Belur, Halebid and Somnathpur.

sections.title: Long answer question. Answer in 70–80 words.

questions.q: Write a note on Benode Behari Mukherjee and his mural 'The Mediaeval Saints'.
questions.answer: Benode Behari Mukherjee (1904–80), a student of Nandalal Bose, loved nature, learnt landscape from Japan and used simple calligraphic lines. Weak-eyed since childhood and finally blind, he still created a huge mural at Kala Bhavan. 'The Mediaeval Saints' (1947) on the wall of Hindi Bhavan, Visva-Bharati, is a Fresco Buono wall painting of saints of different religions as huge elongated figures in flowing rhythm, balanced by smaller figures of common people, in brown, yellow ochre and terraverte.
